group.passage: Dogs and cats are among the most popular pets today, yet they came to share our homes in surprisingly different ways. By studying ancient bones and DNA, scientists have pieced together much of what happened, although some parts of the story are still being argued over. The two texts below describe how each animal made its journey.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Dogs
passage_parts.text: Every dog alive today, from the tiny Chihuahua to the giant Great Dane, comes from a population of ancient wolves that no longer exists. Most experts agree that the partnership began while people were still hunting and gathering, long before anyone planted crops. Exactly how it started, however, is still hotly debated. Some scientists believe that the boldest wolves began following human groups to feed on leftover meat, slowly losing their fear of people; others think that hunters took wolf pups from their dens and raised them by hand. Either way, the animals got a steady supply of food, and people gained skilled partners for the hunt. Much later, people began breeding dogs for particular jobs, such as herding sheep, pulling sleds, or simply keeping people company. As a result, few animals on Earth are as varied in appearance as the modern dog.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Cats
passage_parts.text: The story of the cat is far less disputed, and it begins with farming. When people in the Middle East first settled down to grow grain, the grain they stored attracted hungry mice, and the mice in turn drew wildcats in from the surrounding deserts. Early grain growers soon realized that these skilled hunters were protecting their harvests, so they let them stay. In this sense, the cat more or less tamed itself: nobody had to capture it or teach it anything, and the arrangement suited both sides, since the cats enjoyed an endless supply of mice while the farmers lost far less of their grain. Because people wanted cats mainly for catching mice, which they already did brilliantly, there was little reason to breed them for other purposes. That is why a typical house cat still looks much like its wild ancestor, and why so many cats keep an independent streak, coming to us only when they please.

translation_zh.text:
狗和貓是今天最受歡迎的寵物之一，但牠們走進我們家中的方式卻出奇地不同。科學家研究古代的骨骸和 DNA，已經拼湊出大部分的經過，不過故事中有些部分仍有爭議。下面兩篇短文分別描述這兩種動物走過的路。

A　狗
今天所有的狗，從小小的吉娃娃到巨大的大丹犬，都來自一群已經不存在的古代狼。多數專家同意，這段夥伴關係始於人類還在狩獵採集、遠在有人種植作物之前。然而它究竟是怎麼開始的，至今仍爭論不休。有些科學家認為，最大膽的狼開始跟著人群吃剩下的肉，慢慢不再怕人；另一些人則認為，是獵人把狼崽從巢穴帶走，親手養大。無論是哪一種，動物得到了穩定的食物來源，人類則多了打獵的好幫手。很久以後，人類開始為特定工作培育狗，例如趕羊、拉雪橇，或只是陪伴人。因此，地球上很少有動物的外觀像現代的狗這樣多樣。

B　貓
貓的故事爭議就少得多，而且要從農耕說起。中東的人最初定居下來種穀物時，他們儲存的穀物引來飢餓的老鼠，老鼠又把周圍沙漠裡的野貓吸引過來。早期種穀物的人很快發現，這些厲害的獵手正在保護他們的收成，於是讓牠們留下。從這個意義上說，貓多少是自己馴化了自己：沒有人需要去抓牠或教牠任何事，而且這樣的安排對雙方都合適，因為貓有吃不完的老鼠，農夫損失的穀物也少了很多。由於人們要貓主要是為了抓老鼠，而這本來就是牠們的拿手本領，所以沒什麼理由為其他目的培育牠們。這就是為什麼一般的家貓看起來仍很像牠的野生祖先，也是為什麼那麼多貓都保有獨立的個性，只在自己高興的時候才來找我們。

problems: 「people gained skilled partners for the hunt」（早期的狗是打獵夥伴）不在事實單內，只能由 f6（後來培育狗打獵）間接支持；內容屬主流說法、沒有錯，但多選正解 E 依賴這句，建議人工審核時確認，之後補進事實單
「The story of the cat is far less disputed」不在事實單內（屬比較性的概括），建議補事實或人工確認
